THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Heard the learned counsel appearing for the respective parties.

2. This appeal is filed challenging the judgment and decree passed in LAC No.181/2010 dated 10.06.2014 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Kunigal wherein compensation of Rs.8,32,000/- per acre is fixed when the property of the appellant is acquired to the extent of 61 guntas of land for Bangalore-Hassan railway broad gauge line construction.
There is no dispute with regard to the acquisition but dispute is only with regard to the awarding of compensation.

The Land Acquisition Officer has granted only an amount of Rs.2,87,496/- at the first instance and hence, reference was made before the Trial Court and the Trial Court granted the amount of Rs.8,32,000/- per acre and also passed an order to pay Rs.1,63,000/- towards 34 Coconut trees and Rs.4,000/- towards 2 Neem trees in Sy.No.48/5A and Rs.9,000/- towards 3 Ala trees, Rs.1,000/- towards 4 Ankale trees, Rs.200/- towards 1 Honge tree in Sy.No.48/7A.
The Trial Court also granted Rs.1,000/- towards one Bamboo Bush, Rs.500/- towards one Ankale tree and Rs.2,000/- towards one Jali tree in Sy.No.48/3A.

The Trial Court also granted Rs.10,000/- towards 3 Ala trees, Rs.20,000/- towards 2 Tamarind trees, Rs.5,000/- towards 2 Neem trees, Rs.1,500/-
towards 3 Honge trees and Rs.25,000/- towards income by raising crops. Being aggrieved by the said order, the present appeal is filed.

sentences.text: The learned counsel appearing for the appellant would vehemently contend that when the documents at NC: 2024:KHC:6688 Ex.P1 and P2 of Beerganahalli are placed before the Trial Court.

ExP1 is the sale deed of the year 2007 wherein an amount of Rs.58,000/- per gunta was given to 1 guntas as well as Ex.P2 is the sale deed of the year 2009 wherein an amount of Rs.1,10,000/- per gunta was given to 2 guntas.
But the Trial Court fails to consider those two documents.

The counsel also submits that Ex.P3 is the certificate issued by the Yadiyur Gram Panchayat stating that Chakenahalli and Beerganahalli are situated within one kilometer distance and the said villages come under said Gram panchayat.
When such being the case, the Trial Court ought to have considered Ex.P1 and P2 documents.

5. Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 would vehemently contend that Ex.P1 is only to the extent of 1 guntas and Ex.P2 is only to the extent of 2 guntas and the same are smaller extent but in the case on hand, the acquired property is to the extent of 61 guntas.
When such being the case, the sale consideration mentioned in Ex.P1 and P2 cannot be taken into consideration.

The learned counsel appearing for the State would vehemently contend that the Trial Court taken note of the material available on record and also having considered the factual aspects comes to the conclusion that the properties which have been sold under Ex.P1 and P2 are smaller extent i.e., 1 guntas and 2 guntas respectively, thus, the same yardstick cannot be applied in the present case while enhancing the compensation to the extent of 61 guntas.

7. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the respective parties and also on perusal of the material available on record it discloses that there is no dispute with regard to the acquisition of the property to the extent of 61 guntas for the purpose of Bangalore-Hassan railway broad gauge line construction that is for the public purpose.
Ex. P1 and P2 are sale deeds in respect of Beerganahalli which is located within one k.m. from the land which was acquired for the public purpose.

No doubt,
there is a force in the contention of the learned counsel appearing for the NC: 2024:KHC:6688 respondents that the properties were acquired as per Ex.P1 and P2 are only to the extent of 1 guntas and 2 guntas respectively and the same is also a smaller extent and the land acquired in the present case is 61 guntas
hence, the said yardstick cannot be considered in the present case.

However, taking into note of the fact that in the very same year i.e., 2007, transaction was taken place as per Ex.P1 and as per Ex.P2, transaction was taken placed in the year 2009 and the nature of the properties at Ex.P1 and P2 are also dry lands.
The said fact has to be taken note of by the Court.
However, having taken note of the fact that acquired property in the present case is 61 guntas which is larger extent.
Hence, it is appropriate to consider the compensation of Rs.30,000/- per gunta.
If it is taken as Rs.30,000/- per gunta, it comes to Rs.12,00,000/- per acre as against Rs.8,32,000/- per acre as awarded by the Trial Court.
Hence, the same is just and proper to consider the same.
In respect of the trees are concerned, the Trial Court has awarded reasonable consideration considering the nature of the trees.

Under such circumstances, I do not find any error committed NC: 2024:KHC:6688 by the Trial Court with regard to the compensation awarded towards trees and enhancement is made only with regard to the land which was acquired to the extent of 61 guntas at C M Mallikarjunaiah vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83351807/

8. In view of the discussions made above, I pass the following:
ORDER
The appeal is allowed in part.

The judgment and award dated 10.06.2014 passed in LAC No.181/2010 by the Trial Court is modified enhancing the compensation of Rs.12,00,000/- per acre as against Rs.8,32,000/- per acre in favour of the appellant and the appellant is entitled for other statutory benefits.
